image_description: A high-angle close-up of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) resting on a textured grey rock surface. The amphibian displays the characteristic glossy black skin with irregular, vivid yellow patches and spots covering its back, head, and limbs. The body is robust and cylindrical, with short, stout limbs visible. The tail extends towards the upper right, showing the same black and yellow pattern. The skin appears moist and glandular.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible in the lower-left quadrant. It appears broad and consistent with salamander anatomy. While specific glandular texture is hard to resolve at this resolution, the general shape and swelling behind the eye area are consistent with parotoid glands.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is the most prominent feature. High-contrast yellow patterns on a black background are clearly visible and match the species description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Specular highlights on the black skin areas indicate a moist, glossy surface texture, consistent with amphibian skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with four digits on forelimbs and five on hindlimbs; digits are blunt and unwebbed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front left limb is clearly visible with distinct, blunt digits. The rear left limb is also visible. The digit count appears consistent with the species (4 front, 5 rear), though exact counting on the obscured rear right limb is difficult. No webbing is observed.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame at the top right. The tip is not visible, making it impossible to verify the 'rounded tip' or compare the full length to the body.

The front right limb is tucked under the body/chin area. The connection point is slightly ambiguous and soft, lacking clear definition of where the limb meets the torso, which is a common minor issue in AI generation of complex poses.
